Posted November 7, 2007 

Analysis by Richard Cowan  

 

Despite the usual opposition of virtually the entire political establishment, the peasants er, people of Denver voted by a wide margin, over 56%, to make marijuana possession the lowest priority for the Denver police.

 

However as NORML reported last week, in 2005, Denver voters approved an ordinance that sought to abolish civil and criminal penalties for the possession of up to one ounce of marijuana by citizens age 21 and older. However, local police disregarded the municipal ordinance instead electing to enforce state cannabis laws, which mandate a civil fine for minor pot possession offenses. 

 

Congratulations to SaferChoice.org, which led the effort.  

See 

The Strategy of Comparing Risks of Cannabis and Alcohol. When an Old Argument Catches On. Analysis by Richard Cowan 

See 

Even if the Denver police encouraged by the establishment continue to ignore the will of the people, this initiative will still send the right message to the Democratic Presidential candidates, because their 2008 National Convention will be held there next August. 

 

(Ironically, the Republican Convention will be in Minneapolis, Larry Craig's home away from home.)  

 

Finally, I am pleased to announce that I have now made my first NORML AudioStash Podcast talking about the Presidential campaigns and cannabis.  

Here it is, in the format of your choice:
